mainTopic: The third-year tithes, the new year for vows, and the source for tying crops to a year once they reach one-third of their growth.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא: produce from two different years may not be tithed one for the other. In year two of the שמיטה cycle you give מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, and in year three you give מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני. רבי יהושע בן לוי learns from 'שנת המעשר' that only one of the two earlier tithes, מעשר ראשון, continues in year three, so מעשר שני drops out. A הקש to נחלה shows that מעשר ראשון never stops. A second ברייתא brings two different sources for מעשר ראשון: רבי יהודה learns it from 'ובא הלוי', and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns it from נחלה. Next, the גמרא turns to vows. A vow 'for a year' lasts twelve months, but a vow 'for this year' ends at תשרי, because vows follow how people normally speak. Finally, a משנה says grain and olives belong to the year in which they reached one-third of their growth. רב אסי learns this from the פסוק linking שנת השמטה with סוכות. רבי זירא begins to respond, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: Old and new produce cannot be tithed for each other; the year-two and year-three tithes
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its ruling. Produce picked after sunset on ערב ראש השנה belongs to the new year, so it cannot be tithed together with produce from the old year. It then lists which tithes apply in year two and in year three.
steps.simpleTranslation: After sunset, you may not separate תרומה and tithes from one batch for the other, because you never tithe new produce for old or old produce for new. If it was year two moving into year three, year-two produce gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני, and year-three produce gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began earlier. Produce picked after sunset counts as the new year's produce, so the two batches cannot cover each other, and each batch follows its own year's tithe rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each year's crop has its own tithe duties, so you cannot use one year's produce to cover another year's obligation. The example of year two into year three makes this sharp: the second tithe is different in each year (מעשר שני versus מעשר עני). Mixing the two batches would give the wrong tithe.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Produce from different tithe years cannot be tithed for each other. Year two gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר שני; year three gets מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the third-year tithe rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that in year three מעשר עני replaces מעשר שני.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the Torah source behind the year-three rule it just quoted. This sets up the next step, where a source is given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated the rule without a source. The גמרא now wants a פסוק that shows two things: מעשר שני stops in the third year, and מעשר ראשון continues.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (a request for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that in year three מעשר עני replaces מעשר שני.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי: the third year has only one tithe, so מעשר שני drops out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי reads 'שנת המעשר' in דברים 26:12 as a year in which only one of the two tithes of years one and two continues: מעשר ראשון. So the year has מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני, which is added in place of מעשר שני, and מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: 'When you finish tithing all the tithe of your produce in the third year, the year of the tithe.' This means a year with only one tithe. How so? מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני are given, and מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers with a פסוק. The phrase 'the year of the tithe' (one tithe) teaches that in year three מעשר שני is dropped.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ordinary years there are two tithes beyond תרומה. The פסוק calls year three 'the year of the tithe', which he reads as one tithe instead of two: of the two tithes given in years one and two, only מעשר ראשון continues. מעשר שני is removed, and the poor man's tithe is added in its place.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When you finish tithing' (the opening of the פסוק)
'the year of the tithe', singular
How so? How does this work?

steps.confusionAlert: 'Only one tithe' does not mean nothing else is given in year three. Of the two tithes given in years one and two, only מעשר ראשון continues. מעשר עני is then added in place of מעשר שני.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: דברים 26:12, 'שנת המעשר', shows that in year three only one of the two earlier tithes continues, מעשר ראשון, so מעשר שני is cancelled.

steps.title: Maybe מעשר ראשון is also cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The derivation raises a possibility: perhaps 'only one tithe' means even מעשר ראשון stops, leaving only מעשר עני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps it is not so, and even מעשר ראשון is also cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation challenges its own reading. If the year has 'only one tithe', maybe that one tithe is מעשר עני alone. This sets up the next step's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'one tithe' could be read as cancelling everything except מעשר עני. Nothing in the פסוק so far protects מעשר ראשון, so a second source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps it is really only... (raising another possible reading)
also

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is not so, but rather

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַף מַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן נָמֵי יִבְטַל

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 3 that only מעשר שני drops out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Only one tithe' could mean that מעשר ראשון is also gone, leaving just מעשר עני.

steps.title: מעשר ראשון is compared to נחלה, so it never stops
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in במדבר links the לוי's tithe to 'נחלה'. Just as an inheritance has no break, מעשר ראשון has no break and is given every year.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Speak to the לוים and say to them: when you take from בני ישראל the tithe that I gave you from them as your inheritance.' The Torah compares the tithe to an inheritance. Just as an inheritance has no interruption, so too מעשר ראשון has no interruption.
steps.whatsHappening: The derivation answers the challenge with a הקש. מעשר ראשון is called the לוי's 'inheritance', so like an inheritance it continues without a break, every year including year three.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the פסוק calls the tithe 'your inheritance', it shares a key feature of נחלה: it is never interrupted. That blocks the reading from step 4. So the 'one tithe' of year three can only be מעשר ראשון, which continues, while מעשר עני replaces מעשר שני.

keyTerms.meaning: the פסוק teaches (introduces the proof-verse)
the פסוק compared it (a הקש, linking two things in one verse)
inheritance, especially land
interruption, break

steps.whatToRemember: מעשר ראשון is given every single year, because the Torah compares it to נחלה, which has no break. Only מעשר שני switches to מעשר עני in year three.

steps.title: A second ברייתא also learns that מעשר שני is cancelled
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא brings the same derivation from 'כי תכלה לעשר': in year three only one of the two earlier tithes continues, so מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: 'When you finish tithing...' means a year that has only one tithe. How so? מעשר ראשון and מעשר עני are given, and מעשר שני is cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a parallel ברייתא that supports the same first point. This sets up its own challenge and answer in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This part matches רבי יהושע בן לוי word for word. Where the two sources differ is in how they protect מעשר ראשון, which comes in the next steps.

steps.title: The second ברייתא asks: maybe מעשר ראשון is cancelled too
steps.stepSummary: The second ברייתא raises the same possibility, that מעשר ראשון might also be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think that even מעשר ראשון is also cancelled?
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא raises the same worry as before, that 'one tithe' might wipe out מעשר ראשון too. This sets up its answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same gap as in step 4. The ברייתא will close it with a different פסוק.

steps.title: 'ובא הלוי': whenever the לוי comes, give him
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from דברים 14:29, 'ובא הלוי'. Whenever the לוי comes you must give to him, so מעשר ראשון continues every year. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'And the לוי shall come.' Any time he comes, give to him. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The second ברייתא proves from 'ובא הלוי' that the לוי always gets his tithe, even in year three. It names רבי יהודה as the source of this teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי used a הקש to נחלה. This ברייתא instead reads 'ובא הלוי' as 'whenever he comes', with no year left out. Both routes reach the same conclusion: מעשר ראשון is never cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And the לוי shall come' (דברים 14:29)
any time that he comes

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sources that מעשר ראשון never stops: רבי יהושע בן לוי's הקש to נחלה, and רבי יהודה's 'ובא הלוי', meaning whenever the לוי comes, give him.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "And the Levite shall come"—
any time that he comes, give to him.

steps.terutzMaskana: 'ובא הלוי' means whenever he comes, so מעשר ראשון is given every year.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's other source: the tithe is like an inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says we do not need 'ובא הלוי'. Instead, the פסוק calls the לוי's tithe a 'נחלה', and an inheritance never stops, so מעשר ראשון never stops either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: You don't need that source. The פסוק says, 'Speak to the לוים… the tithe which I gave you from them as your inheritance.' The פסוק compared the tithe to an inheritance. Just as an inheritance has no break, so too מעשר ראשון has no break.
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the second ברייתא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagrees with רבי יהודה about which פסוק teaches that מעשר ראשון is given every year, and he offers his own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree on the halacha: in year three only מעשר שני is replaced, and מעשר ראשון continues. They argue only about the source. רבי יהודה learns it from 'ובא הלוי'. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learns it from the comparison to נחלה, the same idea the first ברייתא used.

steps.whatToRemember: Everyone agrees that מעשר ראשון goes to the לוי every single year, including year three. The only argument is which פסוק teaches it.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון is never interrupted, because the פסוק compares it to a נחלה.

steps.title: A vow for 'a year' versus a vow for 'this year'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the new year for vows. A ברייתא rules that a vow 'for a year' lasts twelve months from the day it was made. A vow 'for this year' ends on א׳ תשרי, even if it was made on כ״ט אלול.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And for vows, etc.' The רבנן taught: Someone forbidden by a vow from getting benefit from his friend for a year counts twelve months, from that day to the same day. But if he said 'for this year', even if he made the vow only on כ״ט אלול, once א׳ תשרי arrives, it counts as a year for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains the next item in the original ברייתא, that א׳ תשרי is the new year for vows. It brings a ברייתא showing what this means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording of the vow decides how long it lasts. 'A year' means a full twelve months counted from the day of the vow. 'This year' means the calendar year, which ends at תשרי, so even one day can be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Vows
Someone forbidden by a vow from getting benefit
From day to day: a full count from that date to the same date
It counts for him as a year

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. 'For a year' means twelve full months. 'For this year' ends on א׳ תשרי, so it can be as short as one day.

phrases.english: "And for vows, etc."
The Rabbis taught:
One who is forbidden by a vow from benefit from his friend for a year

phrases.aramaic: מוֹנֶה שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר חוֹדֶשׁ מִיּוֹם לְיוֹם.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow 'for a year' lasts twelve full months. A vow 'for this year' ends on א׳ תשרי.

steps.title: Why one day is enough for a vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the ruling holds even for the view that one day does not count as a year. A person who makes this vow only wanted to suffer, and he has suffered.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says that one day in a year does not count as a year, here it works. He took the vow on himself to make himself suffer, and he has already suffered.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא heads off a possible question: how can a single day in אלול count as 'a year'? It explains that for vows, everyone agrees it can.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold elsewhere that one day is not enough to count as a year. But a vow is about the person's goal. He wanted to hold himself back and feel the hardship, and that already happened. So the vow is fulfilled once the year changes.

steps.terutzMaskana: A vow aims to make the person suffer. He already suffered, so even one day is enough.

steps.title: Why not end the year at ניסן?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a vow 'for this year' ends at תשרי. ניסן is also called a new year, so maybe it should end then.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say the year ends at ניסן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the choice of תשרי as the end of the vow year. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our מסכת lists ניסן as a new year for other things, such as kings and festivals. So 'this year' could mean the year that ends at ניסן. The question asks what makes תשרי the right date for vows.

keyTerms.meaning: But say (suggests a different option)
The month of Nisan, also counted as a new year for some things

phrases.english: But say Nisan?

steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that a vow 'for this year' ends on א׳ תשרי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: ניסן is also a new year, so nothing obvious makes תשרי the deciding date.

steps.title: Vows follow how people normally speak
steps.stepSummary: The answer: vows are understood the way ordinary people use words, and people count 'the year' from תשרי.
steps.simpleTranslation: With vows, we follow the way people normally speak.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the ניסן question with a general rule about vows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A vow means what an ordinary speaker means by those words, not a special legal meaning. In everyday speech the year turns over at תשרי. So 'this year' ends at תשרי, not ניסן.

keyTerms.meaning: Follow (go according to)
The way ordinary people speak

steps.whatToRemember: There is a major rule here: בנדרים הלך אחר לשון בני אדם. A vow is understood the way people commonly speak. That is why the vow year ends at תשרי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule comes up again and again in the laws of vows. It decides what a person's words mean in many different cases.

phrases.english: With vows,
follow the language of people.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּנְדָרִים הַלֵּךְ אַחַר לְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ניסן question from step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A general rule for reading vows: follow everyday speech.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow year might end at ניסן, since ניסן is also a new year.
steps.terutzMaskana: People normally count the year from תשרי, and vows follow normal speech, so the vow year ends at תשרי.

steps.title: A משנה about when crops are tied to a year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה: תלתן counts from when it sprouts, and grain and olives count from when they reach one-third of their growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in a משנה elsewhere: Fenugreek counts from when it sprouts. Grain and olives count from when they reach one-third of their growth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new משנה to discuss. It gives the growth stage at which different crops become connected to a year for מעשרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each crop gets its own marker: תלתן is marked by sprouting, while grain and olives are marked by reaching one-third of full growth. The next steps will explain the first marker and then look for the source of the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Fenugreek, a plant grown for its seeds
From when it sprouts
One-third (of the crop's full growth)

phrases.english: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה somewhere else: מעשרות 1:3, about when produce starts needing מעשרות.

phrases.english: Fenugreek: from when it sprouts,
grain and olives: from when they reach one-third.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The discussion of vows has ended. The גמרא now brings a new source about the year in which produce counts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תלתן counts from sprouting. Grain and olives count from reaching one-third of their growth.

steps.title: What does 'from when it sprouts' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by saying תלתן counts 'from when it sprouts'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'from when it sprouts' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the משנה's phrase about תלתן. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taken simply, 'sprouting' could mean the very first moment the plant comes up out of the ground. The גמרא wants to know exactly which stage of growth the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: What (does it mean)?

phrases.english: What does 'from when it sprouts' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי מִשֶּׁתִּצְמַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact growth stage meant by 'sprouting' for תלתן.

steps.title: It means sprouting for seed
steps.stepSummary: 'Sprouting' means the stage when the seeds of the תלתן are developed enough to grow a new plant.
steps.simpleTranslation: From when it sprouts for seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה means a later stage, when the plant's seeds are developed enough to be planted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the marker for תלתן is not the first green shoot. It is the point when its seeds are able to sprout into a new crop.

keyTerms.meaning: For seeds (seeds able to grow a new plant)

phrases.english: From when it sprouts for seed.
phrases.notes: He means from when its seeds are developed enough that planting them would grow a new plant.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשֶּׁתִּצְמַח לִזְרָעִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the meaning of 'sprouting'.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Sprouting' means sprouting for seed, when the seeds can grow a new plant.

steps.title: What is the source for the one-third rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's rule for grain and olives again and asks where it comes from.
steps.simpleTranslation: Grain and olives count from when they reach one-third. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the second rule in the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the derivation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one-third marker is not obvious, so the גמרא wants a פסוק behind it. The question is why one-third of growth decides which year the crop belongs to.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)
Grain

phrases.english: Grain and olives: from when they reach one-third.
From where do we know these things?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the תלתן rule to asking for the source of the grain and olives rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that one-third of growth sets the crop's year.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן brings a פסוק about שמיטה and סוכות
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי, quoting רבי יוחנן, with the teaching traced back to רבי יוסי הגלילי, cites a פסוק that mentions שנת השמטה together with סוכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן, and some traced it to רבי יוסי הגלילי: The פסוק says, 'At the end of seven years, at the time of the year of release, on the festival of סוכות.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by bringing a פסוק. The next step will point out what is strange about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק joins two things together: שנת השמטה and חג הסוכות. That link is the key the גמרא will use to find the one-third rule.

keyTerms.meaning: And they traced it back (to an earlier teacher)
The year of release, the seventh year (שביעית)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: Rav Asi said that Rabbi Yochanan said,

phrases.aramaic: וּמָטוּ בָּהּ מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: and some traced it to the name of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili:
The verse says:
"At the end of seven years,
at the time of the year of release, on the festival of Sukkot,"

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering 'מנא הני מילי' by bringing a פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק in דברים 31:10, which mentions שנת השמטה together with סוכות.

steps.title: סוכות already falls in the eighth year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out a problem in the פסוק: סוכות comes after ראש השנה, so it is already in the eighth year. Why mention שמיטה there?
steps.simpleTranslation: What does the שמיטה year have to do with סוכות? It is already the eighth year!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק links שמיטה to סוכות. This question sets up the lesson the גמרא will draw out next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The year changes at ראש השנה in תשרי, and סוכות comes two weeks later. So that סוכות is already in the eighth year, not the seventh. Calling it the time of 'the year of release' seems wrong, and that is a sign the פסוק is hinting at something.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it doing here? What does it have to do with this?
The eighth year, the year after שמיטה

phrases.english: What does the year of release have to do
with the festival of Sukkot?
It is the eighth year!
phrases.notes: The new year starts at ראש השנה, so the סוכות right after it already belongs to the next year.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁנַת הַשְּׁמִטָּה מַאי עֲבִידְתֵּיהּ בְּחַג הַסּוּכּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out a puzzle in the wording of the פסוק just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The plain reading of the פסוק, which links שנת השמטה with סוכות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: סוכות falls after ראש השנה, in the eighth year, so it seems wrong to call it part of the שמיטה year.

steps.title: Produce that reached one-third in שביעית keeps its rules
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that grain which reached one-third of its growth in the seventh year, before ראש השנה, is treated with the rules of שביעית even in the eighth year.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is to tell you: any grain that reached one-third in the seventh year before ראש השנה, you treat it with the rules of the seventh year in the eighth year.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the puzzle. The פסוק mentions שמיטה at סוכות to teach that crops which reached one-third in the seventh year still follow שביעית rules in the eighth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some crops are still growing at סוכות of the eighth year, yet they keep the rules of שמיטה because they reached one-third in the seventh. This shows that reaching one-third is what ties a crop to its year. That gives the source for the משנה's rule for grain and olives.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it comes to tell you
The rules of the seventh year (שביעית)

steps.whatToRemember: Reaching one-third of growth fixes which year grain and olives belong to. This is learned from the פסוק that connects שנת השמטה with סוכות of the eighth year.
steps.whyThisMatters: This one-third rule decides which year's laws apply to a crop, both for שביעית and for the year counted for מעשרות.

phrases.english: Rather, it is to tell you:
any grain that reached one-third
in the seventh year, before Rosh HaShanah,

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה נוֹהֵג בּוֹ מִנְהַג שְׁבִיעִית בַּשְּׁמִינִית.
phrases.english: you treat it with the rules of the seventh year in the eighth year.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, לוֹמַר לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the puzzle about סוכות, and in doing so finishes the source for the one-third rule.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the פסוק: the odd link between שמיטה and סוכות is a hint to a new rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק seemed to wrongly place סוכות in the שמיטה year.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that crops which reached one-third in the seventh year keep שביעית rules in the eighth. So one-third of growth sets the crop's year.

steps.title: רבי זירא turns to רב אסי
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא begins to speak to רב אסי about the teaching he just brought.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to רב אסי:
steps.whatsHappening: This is only an opening line. The גמרא is setting up the next move: רבי זירא is about to respond to רב אסי's teaching from Steps 18–20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אסי just used a פסוק to show that grain which reached one-third of its growth before ראש השנה keeps the rules of שביעית. Now רבי זירא, another אמורא, speaks directly to him. This tells us that what comes next is a reaction to that teaching, not a new topic.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a full argument in this line. It only tells you who is speaking to whom. The actual question comes right after it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said to Rav Asi:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי זֵירָא לְרַב אַסִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces רבי זירא's reaction to רב אסי's source and its explanation in Steps 18–20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Not yet stated in this line. The question itself comes next.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אסי's derivation in Steps 18–20 that reaching one-third of growth in the seventh year ties grain to שביעית.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not stated on this amud. Only the opening line appears here, and רבי זירא's actual challenge comes on the next amud.
